views.name: users_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  DisplayName,
  Reputation,
  CreationDate,
  LastAccessDate,
  Location,
  AccountId
FROM users
views.description: Canonical, cleaned projection of users exposing primary identifiers and profile/reputation fields used for comparisons and joins.

views.name: users_by_displayname_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  DisplayName,
  Reputation,
  AccountId
FROM users_core
views.description: Subset/cohort of users keyed by DisplayName to support direct comparisons or lookups by exact display name (one row per user). Does not deduplicate display names — keeps all users with the same DisplayName for downstream disambiguation.

views.name: users_core_2
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId,
  users.Location AS Location,
  users.ProfileImageUrl AS ProfileImageUrl
FROM users
views.description: One-row-per-user canonical user projection with key identifiers and common profile/date fields normalized for downstream filtering and joins.

views.name: posts_with_owner
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id",
  posts.OwnerUserId AS "posts.OwnerUserId",
  posts.Title AS "posts.Title",
  posts.CreaionDate AS "posts.CreaionDate",
  posts.PostTypeId AS "posts.PostTypeId",
  posts.Tags AS "posts.Tags",
  users.Id AS "users.Id as Owner_Id",
  users.DisplayName AS "users.DisplayName as Owner_DisplayName",
  users.CreationDate AS "users.CreationDate as Owner_CreationDate"
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId
views.description: Posts joined to their owner user key and basic post attributes to support questions linking posts and users.

views.name: user_badge_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(badges.Id) AS badge_count,
  MAX(badges.Date) AS latest_badge_date,
  MIN(badges.Id) AS badges_min_id
FROM badges
GROUP BY badges.UserId
views.description: Per-user badge counts and latest badge date; useful to filter or rank users by badge activity.

views.name: users_core_5
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  DisplayName,
  CreationDate,
  LastAccessDate,
  Reputation,
  AccountId
FROM users
WHERE Id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical, cleaned projection of the users table exposing identity, access, and basic profile attributes. Use this as the base user cohort for filters, counts, joins and time-based queries.

views.name: posts_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount
FROM posts
WHERE posts.Id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical projection of posts exposing post identity, type, ownership, timestamps and tag/title metadata. Useful for linking activity to users and for time- or tag-based cohorting.

views.name: user_badges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(*) AS badge_count,
  MAX(b.Date) AS most_recent_badge_date
FROM badges AS b
WHERE b.UserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY b.UserId
views.description: Per-user aggregation of badges: counts and most recent badge date. Useful to enrich user cohorts with badge-derived features (activity/recognition).

views.name: posts_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.OwnerDisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical projection of posts with normalized key columns and primary display/owner fields. Keeps owner id and owner display name (may be null) and core post metadata useful for filtering by title, tags, or id.

views.name: users_core_9
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  DisplayName,
  Reputation,
  CreationDate
FROM users
views.description: Canonical projection of users exposing identity and primary display name and basic reputation/creation metadata for joins to posts, comments, badges, and votes.

views.name: post_owner_resolution
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS PostId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.OwnerDisplayName AS PostsOwnerDisplayName,
  users.DisplayName AS UsersDisplayName,
  COALESCE(users.DisplayName, posts.OwnerDisplayName) AS ResolvedOwnerDisplayName
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
grain: PostId -- one row per post with owner resolution
views.description: Denormalized view that resolves a post's owner display name: prefer users.DisplayName when OwnerUserId is present, but still expose the original posts.OwnerDisplayName. Useful for queries that need the authoritative owner name and fall back to the stored owner display.

views.name: posts_by_owner
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags
FROM posts
views.description: Row-level view of posts with their owner user id and common post attributes useful for filtering, grouping and counting posts by user.

views.name: users_core_12
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM users
views.description: Canonical user rows exposing primary identifiers and display attributes for joins and filters on user identity.

views.name: posts_with_owner_13
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id",
  posts.OwnerUserId AS "posts.OwnerUserId",
  posts.Title AS "posts.Title",
  posts.CreaionDate AS "posts.CreationDate",
  posts.Score AS "posts.Score",
  users.Id AS "users.Id as UserId",
  users.DisplayName AS "users.DisplayName"
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users
  ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
views.description: Denormalized view joining posts to their owner user row (if present) to simplify queries that need post + owner attributes.

views.name: posts_core_14
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  Title,
  OwnerUserId,
  LastEditorUserId,
  AcceptedAnswerId,
  ParentId,
  PostTypeId,
  Score,
  ViewCount,
  Tags,
  CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  LastEditDate
FROM posts
views.description: One-row-per-post core attributes useful for filtering and joining (title, owners, editors, parent/accepted info and basic counts). Keep raw values for later filtering/aggregation.

views.name: users_core_15
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  users.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate,
  users.Location AS Location
FROM users
views.description: One-row-per-user with identifying and profile fields commonly needed for display and joins (display name, reputation, account id, activity dates).

views.name: posts_with_last_editor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS post_Id,
  posts.Title AS post_Title,
  posts.LastEditDate AS post_LastEditDate,
  posts.LastEditorUserId AS post_LastEditorUserId,
  users.Id AS editor_Id,
  users.DisplayName AS editor_DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS editor_Reputation
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users
  ON posts.LastEditorUserId = users.Id
views.description: Denormalized post rows joined to their last editor user row (if any). Exposes post identifiers and the last editor's user id and display name to simplify queries about who last edited which post.

views.name: users_basic_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.Age AS Age,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation
FROM users
views.description: Canonical, cleaned user-level attributes used for filtering and joins. Exposes primary key and commonly filtered demographic/profile fields with normalized column names.

views.name: posts_core_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: Row-level posts with core identifying and metric columns used for filtering, joining, and aggregation. Keeps one row per post and exposes owner link and score/view counts.

views.name: posts_with_owner_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id",
  posts.OwnerUserId AS "posts.OwnerUserId",
  posts.Score AS "posts.Score",
  posts.Title AS "posts.Title",
  users.Id AS "users.Id AS user_Id",
  users.Age AS "users.Age",
  users.DisplayName AS "users.DisplayName",
  users.Reputation AS "users.Reputation"
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId
views.description: Denormalized view joining posts to their owner user profile to support queries that filter posts by owner attributes (age, reputation, location). One row per post enriched with owner fields.

views.name: tags_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tags.Id AS Id,
  tags.TagName AS TagName,
  tags.Count AS Count,
  tags.ExcerptPostId AS ExcerptPostId,
  tags.WikiPostId AS WikiPostId
FROM tags
views.description: One-row-per-tag core attributes to support lookups by tag name and joins to posts (holds tag identifiers and linked post ids).

views.name: posts_basic_21
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.AcceptedAnswerId AS AcceptedAnswerId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.Body AS Body,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,

FROM posts
views.description: Canonical post rows with primary identifiers, ownership, lifecycle dates and text fields. Normalizes/renames columns for consistent use (keeps raw measures like Score, ViewCount).

views.name: tags_to_excerpt_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tags.Id AS TagId,
  tags.TagName AS TagName,
  tags.ExcerptPostId AS ExcerptPostId,
  tags.WikiPostId AS WikiPostId
FROM tags
views.description: Denormalized mapping of tags to their excerpt post (and wiki post) including tag name and the referenced post id(s), enabling easy retrieval of the referenced post rows.

views.name: users_core_23
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId,

FROM users
views.description: Basic user rows exposing identity and common attributes for joins and filtering by display name or id.

views.name: posts_core_24
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags
FROM posts
WHERE posts.Id IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per post with owner linkage and raw measures (score, counts, timestamps, title/tags) for filtering, grouping, and aggregation.

views.name: posts_core_25
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,
  posts.CommentCount AS CommentCount,
  posts.FavoriteCount AS FavoriteCount
FROM posts
WHERE posts.Id IS NOT NULL
views.description: One-row-per-post core attributes relevant for analysis (identifiers, score, owner, basic counts and tags). Filters only remove rows that are clearly deleted via NULL id if needed; otherwise no business-specific filtering.

views.name: users_core_26
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.Age AS Age,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM users
views.description: Canonicalized user attributes used to characterize owners (identifiers, demographic/engagement metrics). Casts or normalizes types and exposes Age for elder determination.

views.name: posts_with_owner_27
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS post_id,
  posts.Score AS post_score,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS owner_user_id,
  users.Age AS owner_age,
  CASE WHEN users.Id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS owner_exists
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
grain: posts.Id  -- one row per post, joined to owner user if present
views.description: Denormalized join of posts to their owner user row (if any). Keeps posts even when there is no matching user (LEFT JOIN) to allow counting posts with missing owners separately.

views.name: comments_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.Score AS Score,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName
FROM comments
views.description: Canonical comment-level rows with key identifiers and common filterable attributes (one row per comment). Useful as the base cohort for queries that start from comments.

views.name: posts_core_29
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.AcceptedAnswerId AS AcceptedAnswerId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,

  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,

  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,

  posts.FavoriteCount AS FavoriteCount,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical post-level rows exposing identifiers, owner, counts and tag/title metadata. Normalize column naming issues (ex. fix 'CreaionDate' misspelling) and expose measures used in analytics (views, score, favorite count, answer/comment counts).

views.name: commented_posts_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS "comments.Id as CommentId",
  comments.PostId AS "comments.PostId as PostId",
  comments.UserId AS "comments.UserId as CommenterUserId",
  comments.CreationDate AS "comments.CreationDate as CommentCreationDate",
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id as PostId",
  posts.FavoriteCount AS "posts.FavoriteCount",
  posts.Title AS "posts.Title",
  posts.OwnerUserId AS "posts.OwnerUserId",
  posts.CreaionDate AS "posts.CreationDate as PostCreationDate"
FROM comments
JOIN posts ON posts.Id = comments.PostId
grain: one row per comment (comments.Id) with post attributes
views.description: Denormalized relation joining comments to their posts and post owners. One row per comment enriched with the post's key attributes to simplify queries that need comment + post context.

views.name: comments_core_31
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.Score AS Score,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName
FROM comments
views.description: Core comment rows with their identifying and linking columns; canonicalized creation date for filtering and analysis.

views.name: posts_core_32
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.AcceptedAnswerId AS AcceptedAnswerId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreaionDate,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,

  posts.FavoriteCount AS FavoriteCount,

  posts.ClosedDate AS ClosedDate,

FROM posts
views.description: Post-level core attributes including status (ClosedDate) and owner/linking columns useful to determine post lifecycle and joins to comments/votes/tags.

views.name: comment_post_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS CommentId,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS CommentUserId,
  comments.CreationDate AS CommentCreationDate,
  comments.Text AS CommentText,
  posts.ClosedDate AS PostClosedDate,
  posts.Title AS PostTitle,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS PostOwnerUserId
FROM comments
JOIN posts ON posts.Id = comments.PostId
views.description: Denormalized view joining comments to their posts to expose comment info alongside the post's lifecycle attributes (including ClosedDate), suitable for checking post status for specific comments.

views.name: users_core_34
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id AS user_id,
  DisplayName AS display_name,
  Reputation AS reputation,
  CreationDate AS creation_date
FROM users
views.description: Canonical user table projection exposing stable user identifiers and display metadata for joins and filters. Normalizes column names and exposes key attributes used for lookups (DisplayName) and joins (Id).

views.name: posts_core_35
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS post_id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS owner_user_id,
  posts.PostTypeId AS post_type_id,
  posts.CreaionDate AS creation_date,
  posts.Score AS score,
  posts.ViewCount AS view_count,
  posts.Title AS title
FROM posts
views.description: Row-level posts projection exposing post identifiers, ownership, timestamps and basic counters. Useful as the base cohort for counts, filters by owner, date ranges, tags and other aggregations.

views.name: users_with_post_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS user_id,
  u.DisplayName AS display_name,
  COUNT(p.Id) AS post_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN posts p
  ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
GROUP BY
  u.Id,
  u.DisplayName
views.description: Aggregated counts of posts per user. Produces one row per user with the raw post_count measure; keeps user id and display name for easy filtering and joining by display name or id.

views.name: votes_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostId,
  VoteTypeId,
  CreationDate,
  UserId,
  BountyAmount
FROM votes
views.description: One row per vote with core vote attributes and foreign keys to related entities. Useful as the base cohort for questions about specific votes, vote counts, or joining votes to users/posts.

views.name: users_core_38
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  users.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate,
  users.Location AS Location,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users
views.description: One row per user with common display and profile attributes. Useful to look up display name, reputation or other user metadata when joining from other entities (posts, votes, comments).

views.name: vote_with_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  votes.Id AS "votes.Id",
  votes.PostId AS "votes.PostId",
  votes.VoteTypeId AS "votes.VoteTypeId",
  votes.CreationDate AS "votes.CreationDate",
  votes.UserId AS "votes.UserId",
  votes.BountyAmount AS "votes.BountyAmount",
  users.DisplayName AS "users.DisplayName",
  users.Reputation AS "users.Reputation",
  users.AccountId AS "users.AccountId"
FROM votes
LEFT JOIN users ON votes.UserId = users.Id
grain: votes.Id -- one row per vote (joined user may be NULL if no UserId)
views.description: Denormalized view joining votes to the user who cast them, exposing vote fields together with user display and id. Useful for retrieving the display name or other user info for a given vote or aggregating votes by user.

views.name: posts_core_40
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,

  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.Title AS Title,

  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,
  posts.CommentCount AS CommentCount,
  posts.FavoriteCount AS FavoriteCount
FROM posts
views.description: One-row-per-post core attributes useful for filtering, counting, and joining to users, votes, comments, and post links.

views.name: votes_core_41
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostId,
  UserId,
  VoteTypeId,
  CreationDate,
  BountyAmount
FROM votes
views.description: One-row-per-vote core attributes useful for counting and joining to posts and users.

views.name: user_activity_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS UserId,
  COALESCE(p.post_count, 0) AS post_count,
  COALESCE(v.vote_count, 0) AS vote_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT OwnerUserId AS UserId, COUNT(*) AS post_count
  FROM posts
  WHERE OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY OwnerUserId
) p ON p.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT UserId AS UserId, COUNT(*) AS vote_count
  FROM votes
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) v ON v.UserId = u.Id
views.description: Per-user aggregated counts of posts and votes (raw counts kept separate). This view aggregates posts and votes by user but does not apply user-specific literals so it can be filtered later.

views.name: posts_core_43
views.body_sql:
SELECT

  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,

  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.LasActivityDate AS LasActivityDate,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,

views.name: posts_with_owner_44

SELECT
  posts.Id AS PostId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.OwnerDisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName,

views.name: comments_core_45
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.Score AS Score,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,

views.description: One-row-per-comment core projection with primary identifiers, text, scores, creation time and linking columns to posts and users. Useful as the base cohort for filters by score, user, post, or date.

views.name: post_comment_join

views.name: user_comment_activity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(comments.Id) AS comment_count,
  AVG(comments.Score) AS avg_comment_score,
  MAX(comments.CreationDate) AS last_comment_date
FROM comments
WHERE comments.UserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY comments.UserId
views.description: Aggregate measures of comment activity per user: total comments, average score, most recent comment date. Useful for ranking or filtering users by comment behavior.

views.name: comments_core_48
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName

views.description: One-row-per-comment core relation exposing comment identifiers, text, creation time and linking keys to posts and users. Useful as the base cohort for any comment-level filters and joins.

views.name: users_core_49
views.body_sql:

views.name: comment_with_user

views.name: posts_core_51

  Id,

  Title,
  OwnerUserId,
  Body,
  Tags,

views.name: users_core_52
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users
views.description: User identity rows exposing display name and reputation and core profile identifiers used to join to posts, comments, badges, and votes.

views.name: posts_with_owner_53
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS PostId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  users.DisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS OwnerReputation
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId
views.description: Denormalized view joining posts to their owner user to expose post attributes alongside the owner's display name and reputation for answering author attribution questions.

views.name: posts_core_54
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.OwnerDisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.AcceptedAnswerId AS AcceptedAnswerId,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,
  posts.CommentCount AS CommentCount,
  posts.FavoriteCount AS FavoriteCount,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.LastEditDate AS LastEditDate,
  posts.LasActivityDate AS LastActivityDate,
  posts.Tags AS Tags
FROM posts
views.description: One-row-per-post core attributes needed for most post-centric queries (identifiers, title, owner info, counts, dates, tags, parent/accepted answer references).

views.name: users_core_55
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  users.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate,
  users.Location AS Location,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users
views.description: One-row-per-user core attributes used for resolving display names and basic user metadata.

views.name: posts_with_owner_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.OwnerDisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName,
  users.DisplayName AS UserDisplayName
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
grain: posts.Id -- one row per post, joined (left) to users on posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
views.description: Denormalized post rows augmented with resolved owner name from users when OwnerUserId is present; exposes both posts.OwnerDisplayName and users.DisplayName for fallback logic.

views.name: posts_core_57
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Body AS Body,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.LastEditDate AS LastEditDate
FROM posts
views.description: Normalized projection of posts with canonical key columns and commonly used metadata (one row per post). Cleans common typos in column names and exposes text fields and owner links.

views.name: comments_core_58
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.Score AS Score,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM comments
views.description: Normalized projection of comments exposing primary keys, linking fields to posts and users, text, score and creation timestamp (one row per comment).

views.name: posthistory_edits_by_post_and_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostId,
  UserId,
  PostHistoryTypeId,
  CreationDate,
  Text,
  RevisionGUID
FROM postHistory
grain: postHistory.Id  -- one row per post history record
views.description: Cohort of postHistory rows that represent edits, exposing PostId and UserId so callers can find which users edited which posts (one row per postHistory entry).

views.name: votes_with_bounty_and_user_post_refs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  votes.Id AS Id,
  votes.PostId AS PostId,
  votes.UserId AS UserId,
  votes.VoteTypeId AS VoteTypeId,
  votes.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  votes.BountyAmount AS BountyAmount
FROM votes
views.description: One row per vote including bounty amount and foreign keys to the post and user; useful as a base cohort for analyzing bounty votes and joining to posts/users.

views.name: posts_core_61
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical projection of posts exposing id, title, owner, parent relation, and text/tags for filtering and grouping. Cleaned/normalized key columns used for text filters and joins.

views.name: users_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  uc.Id AS Id,
  uc.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  uc.Reputation AS Reputation,
  uc.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users_core AS uc
views.description: Primary user identity projection exposing id, display name and basic profile fields used for attribution and display.

views.name: posts_core_63
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical row-level representation of posts with key identifiers, text fields, tags and view/score metrics. Normalizes column names and exposes values used for filtering, grouping and joins.

views.name: comments_by_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.UserId AS UserId
FROM comments
views.description: All comments annotated with the post they belong to; preserves comment text and basic metadata for joining to posts and aggregations.

views.name: post_viewcount_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS PostId,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  AVG(posts.ViewCount) OVER () AS AverageViewCount_per_cohort
FROM posts
WHERE posts.ViewCount IS NOT NULL
views.description: Per-post aggregated measures for posts (e.g., average/summary of ViewCount). Keeps one row per post with raw and aggregated view metrics to support higher-level summaries.

views.name: badges_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  UserId,
  Name,
  Date
FROM
  badges
views.description: All badge records from the badges table, canonicalized for downstream use. Keeps original badge attributes and excludes rows with NULL UserId only if caller requests; otherwise all rows are exposed so callers can apply their own NULL filters.

views.name: badges_per_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  UserId,
  COUNT(*) AS badge_count,
  MIN(Date) AS first_awarded,
  MAX(Date) AS last_awarded
FROM badges
GROUP BY UserId
views.description: Aggregate count of badges per user. One row per UserId with the raw badge_count and optional earliest/latest award dates; callers apply thresholds or join to users as needed.

views.name: users_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  DisplayName,
  Reputation,
  CreationDate
FROM users_core
views.description: Canonical user dimension with primary identifiers and common attributes useful for filtering or joining (reputation, display name, creation date).

views.name: posts_core_69
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
WHERE posts.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
views.description: One-row-per-post core attributes and ownership information. Keeps canonical numeric/date fields and explicit owner linkage; useful for filtering by owner, views, scores, tags, and parent/answer relationships.

views.name: post_history_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  postHistory.PostId AS PostId,
  COUNT(postHistory.Id) AS posthistory_count
FROM postHistory
GROUP BY postHistory.PostId
views.description: Number of postHistory records per post. Useful to determine posts with zero, one, or many history entries and to apply per-post history-count filters.

views.name: users_basic_71
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users_core.Id AS Id,
  users_core.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users_core.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users_core.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM users_core
views.description: Basic user identity and profile fields for join targets and display. Exposes primary keys and display name used by most user-level queries.

views.name: badges_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.Id AS Id,
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  badges.Name AS Name,
  badges.Date AS Date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', badges.Date) AS INTEGER) AS year
FROM badges
views.description: Canonicalized badge rows with stable id and parsed year for the badge Date. Keeps raw columns needed for badge-level filtering and grouping.

views.name: badges_by_name_and_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.Id AS Id,
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  badges.Name AS Name,
  badges.Date AS Date,
  strftime('%Y', badges.Date) AS year,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY badges.Name, strftime('%Y', badges.Date)) AS badge_count
FROM badges
views.description: Aggregated counts of badges grouped by badge name and year. Useful for computing shares or year-over-year changes for specific badge names.

views.name: badge_totals_by_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Name,
  COUNT(*) AS total_count
FROM badges
GROUP BY Name
views.description: Total badge counts per badge name across all years. Useful to calculate denominators when computing shares for a particular name.

views.name: user_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.UpVotes AS UpVotes,
  users.Age AS Age
FROM users
views.description: One-row-per-user canonical user record exposing identifiers and core attributes used for aggregations (reputation, upvotes, age) and join keys to posts.

views.name: posts_per_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COUNT(posts.Id) AS post_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(posts.AnswerCount,0)) AS answer_count_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(posts.ViewCount,0)) AS viewcount_sum
FROM posts
WHERE posts.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY posts.OwnerUserId
views.description: Aggregated post counts and basic post-level totals per owner user. Keeps one row per OwnerUserId with raw counts and sums so callers can filter by number of posts or compute rates.

views.name: votes_with_normalized_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  votes.Id AS Id,
  votes.PostId AS PostId,
  votes.VoteTypeId AS VoteTypeId,
  votes.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  CASE
    WHEN votes.CreationDate IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(strftime('%Y', votes.CreationDate) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS year,
  CASE
    WHEN votes.CreationDate IS NOT NULL THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS has_creation_date
FROM votes

semantic_filters.None: no filter (all rows preserved); NULL CreationDate rows are included but marked via has_creation_date = 0

views.description: Normalized projection of the votes table that exposes each vote row with its raw CreationDate plus derived year and a canonical non-null flag. Keeps one row per vote.

views.name: votes_by_year_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  COUNT(Id) AS vote_count,
  MAX(Id) AS Id -- carry primary key of source table to keep joinable
FROM votes
WHERE CreationDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Aggregates vote counts per year (derived from CreationDate). Produces one row per year with the count of votes in that year. Useful for year-over-year comparisons and ratios.

views.name: votes_with_post_and_user_refs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  votes.Id AS Id,
  votes.PostId AS PostId,
  votes.UserId AS UserId,
  votes.VoteTypeId AS VoteTypeId,
  votes.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM votes

semantic_filters.None: no filter; preserve all vote rows

views.description: Denormalized view exposing votes with their PostId and UserId references (joins kept implicit by exposing keys). Useful when correlating votes with post or user attributes in downstream queries.

views.name: users_core_80
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users
views.description: One-row-per-user core user attributes for joins and filters (canonicalized display name and id).

views.name: posts_core_81
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: One-row-per-post core attributes including owner link and measures (AnswerCount, Score, ViewCount) used for ranking and filtering.

views.name: user_posts_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS post_Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS post_OwnerUserId,
  posts.AnswerCount AS post_AnswerCount,
  posts.Score AS post_Score,
  posts.ViewCount AS post_ViewCount,
  posts.Title AS post_Title,
  posts.CreaionDate AS post_CreationDate,
  users.Id AS user_Id,
  users.DisplayName AS user_DisplayName
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users
  ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
grain: posts.Id  -- one row per post (with its owner user info)
views.description: Denormalized view joining users to their posts to support queries that select or rank a user's posts by post measures.

views.name: users_core_83
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM users
views.description: Canonical row-level view of users exposing identity and display attributes used for joins and filtering. NULLs preserved.

views.name: posts_core_84
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  COALESCE(posts.ViewCount, 0) AS ViewCount_normalized,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical row-level view of posts exposing ownership, view counts and identifying columns. Normalizes ViewCount NULLs to 0 for reliable aggregation and exposes OwnerUserId for joining to users.

views.name: user_post_views
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS UserId,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  posts.Id AS PostId,
  -- normalize ViewCount: coalesce to 0 for missing, cast to real and divide by NULLIF(1,0) placeholder
  -- actual normalization strategy: expose per-post viewcount as-is but named ViewCount_normalized so downstream can apply cohort normalization
  COALESCE(posts.ViewCount, 0) AS ViewCount_normalized
FROM users
JOIN posts ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
grain: UserId, PostId  -- one row per post owned by a user
views.description: Denormalized view joining users to their posts, with post view counts normalized so downstream queries can aggregate per user easily.
